cause: After SIGTERM, ss can report the closing listener PID just as /proc removes the process. A previously readable listener then raises listener-identity-unreadable during the bounded close wait. The former handler tolerated listener-owner-ambiguous only and refused early; no successor was started.
method: The exact old source fragment at testedCommit was replaced once by syntax-valid new text that removed only the post-SIGTERM unreadable-identity allowance. The focused Vitest command executed one real private-listener test and exited 1 at its injected third-inspection assertion. apply_patch restored the source; the complete restart suite then exited 0 with 8/8 tests and the worktree was clean.

mutation.old:
if (!(error instanceof RestartRefusal)
          || (error.code !== 'listener-owner-ambiguous' && error.code !== 'listener-identity-unreadable')) throw error;
mutation.new:
if (!(error instanceof RestartRefusal)
          || error.code !== 'listener-owner-ambiguous') throw error;
mutation.command: npx vitest run --project @syzygy/three-surface-poc-app --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1 --testTimeout=20000 apps/three-surface-poc/src/restart.test.ts -t 'waits through one vanished post-SIGTERM identity' --reporter=dot
mutation.predicate: An unreadable identity only after SIGTERM is polled until socket absence or timeout; it never authorizes a successor while ownership remains unknown.
